title: Without inventory accounts mapped no parts entry is sent, shop supplies still is
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to an expense account, account X, at the test location.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure Inventory Asset is not mapped on the test location's ShopView Accounts page.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2, whose Shop supplies amount is $15.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. In QuickBooks Online, open the journal entries for work order 1's number.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Stock parts row carries the note "Parts cost is not posted to QuickBooks at this location: inventory accounts are not mapped."

Step 3:

  • The work order is Closed.

Step 4:

  • Only the $15.00 shop supplies entry is in QuickBooks; there is no parts entry.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-N5: “If Inventory Asset or Cost of Parts is not mapped at the location, no parts entry is sent at Close (stock parts and reclass entries), as invoicing sends none today for that location: the inventory journal entries need both accounts, so a shop that keeps no inventory in QuickBooks is never credited on Inventory Asset by Close alone. The shop supplies entry of S7-R4a still posts. The Close confirmation shows on the Stock parts and Special orders rows the note "Parts cost is not posted to QuickBooks at this location: inventory accounts are not mapped."”
  • S3-N4: “If no account is mapped for the work order's classification (for a no-charge work order in QuickBooks, no account for the work order's category), the confirmation of S3-R2 replaces the account note with: QuickBooks, "No account set for [category]. The entry posts to the ShopView Review account until you set one." with a "Set account" link to Integrations > QuickBooks; AccountingHub, "No account set for [category]. The entry is held in Accounting Events until you set one." with a link to Account Mappings. The link is shown only to users with 'Settings — Integrations' (QuickBooks) or 'Accounting — Settings' (AccountingHub); others see the note without the link. The Shop supplies row follows the same rule when the Shop supplies item is not mapped (S10-N2). The button still reads "Close Work Order" and closes as in S3-R3. At a QuickBooks location without Inventory Asset or Cost of Parts, the parts rows carry the note of S7-N5 instead.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
